feat(host): start the client as the local Host and persist its identity

Chapter 18 phase A: the computer client is the local Host plus the PWA that
Host serves, so starting it neither needs a JI_* variable nor a second web
server, and the Host identity becomes durable instead of per-process.

Startup entry
- `ji host start [--open-browser]` and the versioned Windows entry
  `ji-start.cmd` (bundled JRE standalone distribution) start the Host and hand
  its one-use launch URI to the default browser. The URI carries no token; a
  machine without a browser falls back to printing the address.
- The startup entry now composes the zero-config Host, so a fresh machine
  reaches a Provider profile it can author in the UI.
- Fix the standalone Windows launcher: the enumerated classpath overflowed the
  cmd.exe 8191-character limit at a deep install path, so the launcher refused
  to start at all. It now uses the JVM classpath wildcard.

Canonical Host identity
- `HostIdentity` + `HostDeviceStore.hostIdentity()/renameHostId()` own the
  persisted hostId and its CAS revision; `HostDeviceRegistry` is the single
  accessor, so the REST projection, local principal, artifact scope, pairing
  acknowledgement and Relay registration key all follow a rename.
- `JI_HOST_ID` becomes a first-write input: it is written once (or a
  `host-<16 hex>` id is generated), validated whenever supplied, and never
  re-identifies a Host that already persisted one. Files written before the
  field existed are backfilled atomically without touching keys or devices.
- `POST /api/v1/host/identity` renames under compare-and-set and returns
  `host.identity_invalid` / `host.identity_revision_conflict` as stable
  structured errors; `GET /api/v1/host` reports `hostIdRevision`.
- Settings -> Host gains the identity control with symmetric en/zh-CN copy.
